question: How many Britons saw the 1939 Keep Calm and Carry On poster on a wall during the war?
options: Hardly any: it was held back
answer: Hardly any. The Ministry of Information printed about 2.45 million copies in 1939 to post after heavy bombing or invasion, never issued them, and most were pulped. A bookseller in Alnwick found one among old books in 2000 and framed it; reprints did the rest. The wartime poster is mostly a twenty-first-century one.
move: The one copy that survived can stand in for a past that never happened.
ask: Which picture of the past do I believe because one copy happened to survive?
trap: It is everywhere now, so it seems it was everywhere then.
source: Lewis, Keep Calm and Carry On, IWM, 2017
reference: Bex Lewis, Keep Calm and Carry On: The Truth Behind the Poster, Imperial War Museum, 2017
